name: Crack Chicken Chili

ingredients.buy: 2 1/2 cups, drained and rinsed (about two 15 oz cans)
4 cups, drained and rinsed (just under two 15 oz cans)
optional: 2/3 cup sour cream, plus avocado or extra cheese, to serve (140 g)

writer_notes: All 17 locked ingredients are used by a step: chicken, bone broth, ranch, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika, chili powder, corn, diced tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans, green chiles and bacon plus cream cheese go into the load step; Mexican blend shredded cheese goes in at the end; sour cream is the optional serve-side topping. No orphans, nothing invented.

Cream cheese is placed in the LOAD step, not the final cheese step. The source instruction says 'combine all ingredients except cheese', but for crack chicken chili the 'except cheese' means only the shredded Mexican blend; cream cheese must go in at the start or it is bought and never used.

FLAG: cayenne scales to 1 tbsp + 1/2 tsp (about 3.5 tsp) across 14 servings. This is faithful to the source (2 tsp x ~1.75 scale) but is a genuinely hot amount; prose calls it spicy and points to the cooling toppings. QA may want to confirm the catalog is fine with that heat level.
Whole recipe scales consistently at ~1.75x from the source (2 lb chicken, 8 oz cream cheese, 10 slices bacon), so no per-line quantity looks off for a 14-serving batch.

No cost_lines were provided in the dispatch, so shop_smart makes no per-ounce or package-longevity claims and carries no dollar figure; cost closing uses only the ${{cost_ps}} token plus the standard $1/month membership line.
Macros cited in prose (542 cal, 47.4g protein) are the locked engine figures only; no number was computed or estimated.

prose.intro_html:
Crack Chicken Chili sounds like a dare and eats like a warm blanket. It is the crack chicken idea, ranch, bacon and cream cheese, poured into a pot of chili and left alone to get better while you go live your life. You do almost nothing, which is exactly the kind of cooking I respect.

Here is why it earns a spot in the rotation. Each of the 14 servings lands at 542 calories with 47.4 grams of protein, and it gets there on chicken breast, two kinds of beans and a can of corn instead of anything fancy. That is a lot of real food doing real work. The slow cooker does the rest.
prose.shop_smart:
This one is a pantry run more than a shopping trip, and that is the whole point. Buy the chicken breast in the biggest boneless skinless pack your store sells, since 3 1/2 pounds is the backbone of the batch and freezes fine if you catch it on sale.

The rest is cans and shelf staples. You need corn, diced tomatoes, kidney beans, black beans and green chiles, so read the label sizes against the list before you check out rather than grabbing on autopilot. Grab a ranch seasoning packet or two, a brick and change of cream cheese, and a bag of Mexican blend shredded cheese. Cook your own bacon from a standard pack instead of buying pre-cooked, because you are chopping it into the pot anyway and the crisp is better. Garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika and chili powder are almost certainly already in your cabinet, so check before you double up.
prose.make_it:
This is a dump-and-walk-away recipe, so the method is short and honest.

Put the chicken breast in the slow cooker and pour in the bone broth. Add the ranch seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika and chili powder. Now the cans: drained corn, the diced tomatoes with their juice, drained and rinsed kidney beans, drained and rinsed black beans, and the green chiles. Scatter in the chopped cooked bacon and drop the cream cheese right on top. It looks like a lump now and it will melt into the broth as it goes. Stir once, cover, and cook on high for 4 to 5 hours or on low for 6 to 8.

When you have about 30 minutes left, lift the chicken breasts out, shred them with two forks, and return the meat to the pot to finish. Right before serving, stir in the shredded Mexican blend cheese until it disappears into the chili. A heads up on the heat: this build carries a real dose of cayenne, so it leans spicy. That is what a bowl of sour cream, avocado and a little extra cheese on top is for.
prose.portion_html:
Do not eyeball this. Set your empty container on the scale, hit tare, and weigh the finished chili in the pot first so you know your total. Divide that number by 14, then scoop to that weight in each container. Every lid closes on the same portion, which is the only way the 542 calories and 47.4 grams of protein per serving actually mean anything.

Keep the sour cream, avocado and extra cheese on the side and add them the day you eat, not now. Cold toppings do not survive a week in the fridge, and the chili itself reheats better without them stirred in.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that makes it stick. This whole batch of 14 dinners runs about ${{cost_ps}} per serving, and it is built almost entirely from cans and pantry spices you can buy any week of the year. No seasonal produce, no specialty aisle, no surprises at the register.

That is 14 high-protein dinners handled for less than most people spend on one takeout order, and it took you ten minutes of actual effort.
prose.upsell_html:
Make it once and you will see why it stays in the rotation. It reheats like a champ, it feeds a crowd or a work week, and it costs next to nothing to keep on repeat.

If you want the full stack of recipes, the shopping math and the weekly plans that keep your grocery bill honest, the Thrifty Crew membership is a dollar a month. One pot of chili already paid for the year.

head.description: Crack Chicken Chili made in the slow cooker for meal prep: 14 high-protein servings at 542 calories and 47.4g protein each, built on chicken breast, beans, corn, bacon and cream cheese.
head.keywords: crack chicken chili, slow cooker chili, high protein meal prep, chicken chili, crockpot chicken chili, budget meal prep dinner, ranch chicken chili
steps: Add the chicken breast and bone broth to the slow cooker, then the ranch seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, paprika and chili powder. Add the drained corn, diced tomatoes with their juice, drained and rinsed kidney beans and black beans, the green chiles, the chopped cooked bacon and the cream cheese. Stir once, cover, and cook on high 4 to 5 hours or low 6 to 8 hours.
With about 30 minutes left, lift out the chicken breasts, shred them with two forks, and return the meat to the pot to finish cooking.
Stir in the shredded Mexican blend cheese until it melts fully into the chili.
Weigh and portion into 14 containers, and top each serving with sour cream, avocado, or extra cheese when you eat it.
